bill_text.plain_text:
A bill for an act relating to education; establishing a high school diploma for armed forces veterans; proposing coding for new law in Minnesota Statutes, chapter 127A.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.

[127A.135] HIGH SCHOOL DIPLOMA FOR VETERANS.

Subdivision 1.

Establishment.

The commissioner must establish a high school diploma for veterans and award a standard high school diploma to a qualifying veteran of the armed forces who has not completed high school graduation requirements. The high school diploma may be awarded to an armed forces veteran based on knowledge and experience gained while in service.

Subd. 2.

Qualifying service; application.

(a) The commissioner may award a high school diploma to an eligible veteran under subdivision 3 who has not completed high school graduation requirements and who meets at least one of the following qualifying service criteria:

(1) served in the Korean Conflict;

(2) served in the Vietnam War; or

(3) left a public or nonpublic school located in any state prior to graduation to serve on active duty in the United States armed forces.

(b) A veteran, or a veteran's family posthumously, may apply for the veteran high school diploma in the form and manner prescribed by the commissioner of education. The Departments of Education and Veterans Affairs must work together to assist veterans with the application process for obtaining a diploma.

Subd. 3.

Eligible veteran.

For purposes of this section, an eligible veteran is a veteran who:

(1) either: (i) is a current resident of the state of Minnesota; (ii) was previously enrolled in a high school in this state; or (iii) was a resident of the state of Minnesota at the time of death; and

(2) was honorably discharged from the United States armed forces as verified by the Department of Veterans Affairs.
additions: The commissioner must establish a high school diploma for veterans and award a standard high school diploma to a qualifying veteran of the armed forces who has not completed high school graduation requirements. The high school diploma may be awarded to an armed forces veteran based on knowledge and experience gained while in service.

(2) served in the Vietnam War; or
(3) left a public or nonpublic school located in any state prior to graduation to serve on active duty in the United States armed forces.

(b) A veteran, or a veteran's family posthumously, may apply for the veteran high school diploma in the form and manner prescribed by the commissioner of education. The Departments of Education and Veterans Affairs must work together to assist veterans with the application process for obtaining a diploma.
For purposes of this section, an eligible veteran is a veteran who:

(1) either: (i) is a current resident of the state of Minnesota; (ii) was previously enrolled in a high school in this state; or (iii) was a resident of the state of Minnesota at the time of death; and
(2) was honorably discharged from the United States armed forces as verified by the Department of Veterans Affairs.

bill_text.plain_text:
A bill for an act relating to education; establishing a high school diploma for armed forces veterans; proposing coding for new law in Minnesota Statutes, chapter 127A.

BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF MINNESOTA:

Section 1.

[127A.135] HIGH SCHOOL DIPLOMA FOR VETERANS.

Subdivision 1.

Diploma.

A school district or charter school must, upon a request under subdivision 2, issue a high school diploma to a veteran as defined in section 197.447 who was unable to complete their high school education for reasons related or unrelated to their military service, and who served:

(1) during the Korean Conflict from June 27, 1950, to January 31, 1955; or

(2) during the Vietnam War, either in the country from November 1, 1955, to May 7, 1975, or outside of the country from August 5, 1964, to May 7, 1975.

Subd. 2.

Request.

A veteran may request a diploma on their own behalf, or a family member may make a posthumous request on behalf of a deceased veteran or service member. The school district or charter school may award the diploma based on the veteran's knowledge and experience gained while in service, or the veteran's other relevant lived experience. The school district or charter school may require the veteran or veteran's requestor to provide evidence that the veteran was a Minnesota public school student or is a current Minnesota resident.

Subd. 3.

No report required.

Districts and charter schools are not required to report on diplomas issued under this section.

Subd. 4.

Assistance.

The Minnesota Department of Veterans Affairs and county veteran service officers may provide assistance to districts and charter schools fulfilling these requests, including but not limited to verification of discharge paperwork.
additions: A school district or charter school must, upon a request under subdivision 2, issue a high school diploma to a veteran as defined in section 197.447 who was unable to complete their high school education for reasons related or unrelated to their military service, and who served:
(1) during the Korean Conflict from June 27, 1950, to January 31, 1955; or
(2) during the Vietnam War, either in the country from November 1, 1955, to May 7, 1975, or outside of the country from August 5, 1964, to May 7, 1975.

A veteran may request a diploma on their own behalf, or a family member may make a posthumous request on behalf of a deceased veteran or service member. The school district or charter school may award the diploma based on the veteran's knowledge and experience gained while in service, or the veteran's other relevant lived experience. The school district or charter school may require the veteran or veteran's requestor to provide evidence that the veteran was a Minnesota public school student or is a current Minnesota resident.
Districts and charter schools are not required to report on diplomas issued under this section.

The Minnesota Department of Veterans Affairs and county veteran service officers may provide assistance to districts and charter schools fulfilling these requests, including but not limited to verification of discharge paperwork.
